```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(finalfit)


analysis_data <- read.csv(
  "../data/processed/data.csv",
  na.strings = "",
  check.names = FALSE
)


key_variables <- c("iso", "year")

# Single source of display labels and table sections for every dataset column.
# Rows are listed in the order they appear in the tables.
recode <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                 ~label,                                                   ~group,
  "iso",                "Country (ISO code)",                                     "Identifier",
  "year",               "Year",                                                   "Identifier",
  "matmor",             "Maternal mortality (per 100,000 live births)",           "Mortality outcomes",
  "infmor",             "Infant mortality (per 1,000 live births)",               "Mortality outcomes",
  "neomor",             "Neonatal mortality (per 1,000 live births)",             "Mortality outcomes",
  "un5mor",             "Under-5 mortality (per 1,000 live births)",              "Mortality outcomes",
  "gdp_1000",           "GDP per capita (1,000 USD)",                             "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "oecd",               "OECD member",                                            "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "pop_dens",           "Population density (%)",                                 "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "urban",              "Urban residence (%)",                                    "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "age_dep",            "Age dependency ratio",                                   "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "male_edu",           "Male education (years)",                                 "Socioeconomic and demographic",
  "region",             "Region",                                                 "Geography and environment",
  "temp",               "Temperature (°C)",                                       "Geography and environment",
  "rainfall_1000",      "Rainfall (1,000 mm)",                                    "Geography and environment",
  "Drought",            "Drought",                                                "Geography and environment",
  "Earthquake",         "Earthquake",                                             "Geography and environment",
  "conflict",           "Armed conflict",                                         "Armed conflict",
  "death_sum",          "Battle-related deaths",                                  "Armed conflict",
  "conflict_intensity", "Conflict intensity",                                     "Armed conflict",
  "death_sum_quintile", "Battle-related deaths (quintile)",                       "Armed conflict",
  "any_missingness",    "Any missingness",                                        "Missingness"
)
stopifnot(all(names(analysis_data) %in% recode$var))

variable_labels <- setNames(recode$label, recode$var)
variable_groups <- setNames(recode$group, recode$var)
label_variable <- function(x) {
  labels <- unname(variable_labels[as.character(x)])
  ifelse(is.na(labels), as.character(x), labels)
}

# Use compact, centred tables that stay within the page width in PDF output.
# `groups` gives the section of each row and is used to add section headers.
format_table <- function(x, ..., groups = NULL, notes = NULL, font_size = 8) {
  table <- kableExtra::kbl(x, ..., booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "")

  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    table <- table |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(
        latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"),
        font_size = font_size,
        full_width = FALSE,
        position = "center"
      )
  } else {
    table <- table |>
      kableExtra::kable_styling(
        bootstrap_options = c("condensed", "responsive"),
        full_width = FALSE,
        position = "center"
      )
  }

  if (!is.null(groups)) {
    table <- kableExtra::pack_rows(table, index = table(forcats::fct_inorder(groups)))
  }
  if (!is.null(notes)) {
    table <- kableExtra::footnote(table, general = notes, threeparttable = TRUE,
                                  general_title = "")
  }
  table
}
```



```{r}
#| label: data-prep
#| include: false

# Keep the country code as a character identifier; use numeric types for
# continuous measures and Yes/No factors for binary indicators.
continuous_variables <- intersect(
  c(
    "matmor", "infmor", "neomor", "un5mor", "gdp_1000", "pop_dens",
    "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000", "death_sum"
  ),
  names(analysis_data)
)
binary_variables <- intersect(
  c("oecd", "Drought", "Earthquake", "conflict"),
  names(analysis_data)
)

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    iso = as.character(iso),
    year = as.integer(year),
    across(all_of(continuous_variables), as.numeric),
    across(all_of(binary_variables),
           ~ factor(.x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))),
    region = factor(region),
    # order categories by severity rather than alphabetically
    conflict_intensity = factor(
      conflict_intensity,
      levels = c("No conflict (<25 deaths)", "Minor conflict (25-999 deaths)",
                 "War (>=1,000 deaths)")
    ),
    death_sum_quintile = factor(
      death_sum_quintile,
      levels = c("None (0 deaths)", paste("Positive deaths: quintile", 1:5))
    )
  )

analysis_variables <- intersect(recode$var, setdiff(names(analysis_data), key_variables))

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    any_missingness = factor(
      if_any(all_of(analysis_variables), is.na),
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE), labels = c("Complete", "Incomplete")
    )
  )

n_countries <- n_distinct(analysis_data$iso)
year_range <- range(analysis_data$year)
escape_latex <- function(x) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) gsub("%", "\\%", x, fixed = TRUE) else x
}

n_conflict <- sum(analysis_data$conflict == "Yes")
n_complete <- sum(analysis_data$any_missingness == "Complete")
n_matmor_missing <- sum(is.na(analysis_data$matmor))
n_matmor_missing_late <- sum(is.na(analysis_data$matmor) & analysis_data$year > 2017)

# Summarise `explanatory` variables across the levels of `dependent`, with the
# group sizes in the column headers and a section header for each variable group.
# `level_labels` optionally renames the levels of `dependent` in the headers.
summary_by <- function(dependent, explanatory, cont = "median",
                       level_labels = NULL) {
  summary <- finalfit::summary_factorlist(
    analysis_data,
    dependent = dependent,
    explanatory = explanatory,
    cont = cont,
    total_col = TRUE,
    add_row_totals = TRUE,
    include_row_totals_percent = FALSE,
    row_totals_colname = "N",
    row_missing_colname = "Missing"
  ) |>
    # summary_factorlist only labels the first row of each variable
    mutate(var = na_if(label, "")) |>
    fill(var)

  counts <- table(analysis_data[[dependent]])
  # a country can contribute country-years to more than one column
  country_counts <- tapply(analysis_data$iso, analysis_data[[dependent]], n_distinct)
  level_names <- if (is.null(level_labels)) names(counts) else level_labels
  level_headers <- sprintf("%s\n(n = %d country-years,\n%d countries)", level_names,
                           as.integer(counts), as.integer(country_counts))
  total_header <- sprintf("Total\n(n = %d country-years,\n%d countries)",
                          nrow(analysis_data), n_countries)

  list(
    table = summary |>
      mutate(label = ifelse(label == "", "", label_variable(label))) |>
      select(label, levels, all_of(names(counts)), Total, N, Missing) |>
      # the table is built with escape = FALSE so the headers can wrap
      mutate(across(everything(), escape_latex)),
    col_names = kableExtra::linebreak(
      c("Variable", "", level_headers, total_header, escape_latex("N (%)"), "Missing"),
      align = "c"
    ),
    groups = unname(variable_groups[summary$var])
  )
}

summary_notes <- function(cont = "median") {
  c(
    if (cont == "median") "Continuous variables: median (Q1 to Q3)." else
      "Continuous variables: mean (SD).",
    "Categorical variables: n (column %).",
    "N (%), observations with non-missing data; Missing, observations with missing data.",
    "A country can contribute country-years to more than one column, so country counts do not add up to the total."
  )
}

print_summary <- function(summary, cont = "median", extra_notes = NULL) {
  format_table(
    summary$table,
    col.names = summary$col_names,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = "llrrrrr",
    groups = summary$groups,
    notes = c(summary_notes(cont), extra_notes)
  )
}
```

The analysis dataset contains `r nrow(analysis_data)` country-year observations from `r n_countries` countries between `r year_range[1]` and `r year_range[2]`. Armed conflict was defined as at least 25 battle-related deaths in a country-year and is lagged by one year, so a conflict observed in year *t* is assigned to year *t* + 1. `r n_conflict` country-years (`r round(100 * n_conflict / nrow(analysis_data), 1)`%) were exposed to armed conflict.

@tbl-overview summarises the mortality outcomes and covariates by armed conflict status. @tbl-completecase compares country-years with complete and incomplete data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-overview
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of country-years by armed conflict status in the previous year (armed conflict: at least 25 battle-related deaths)"

# Conflict-derived measures are excluded because they are defined by the
# grouping variable.
conflict_measures <- c("conflict", "death_sum", "conflict_intensity",
                       "death_sum_quintile")
table1_variables <- setdiff(analysis_variables, conflict_measures)

conflict_headers <- c("No conflict", "Armed conflict")

summary_by("conflict", table1_variables, level_labels = conflict_headers) |>
  print_summary()
```


```{r}
#| eval: false
#| label: mean-summary
# To show this table, set eval: true, rename the label to tbl-mean and add
# tbl-cap: "Continuous variables by armed conflict status in the previous year, summarised by mean (SD)"

summary_by("conflict", setdiff(continuous_variables, conflict_measures),
           cont = "mean", level_labels = conflict_headers) |>
  print_summary(cont = "mean")
```

`r n_complete` country-years (`r round(100 * n_complete / nrow(analysis_data), 1)`%) have no missing data. Maternal mortality is the main source of missingness: `r n_matmor_missing_late` of its `r n_matmor_missing` missing values fall after 2017, the last year it was reported.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-completecase
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of country-years by whether any variable is missing"

summary_by("any_missingness", analysis_variables) |>
  print_summary(
    extra_notes = "Complete: no missing values in any variable; Incomplete: at least one missing value."
  )
```
